title: Concept Drills — Work, Energy & Power (Class 11 Physics)
subject: physics

questions.question: A person holds a heavy suitcase motionless for ten minutes and gets tired. Why is the physical work done zero?
questions.solution: Work = F·d·cosθ needs DISPLACEMENT along the force; d = 0 here, so W = 0 — the tiredness is internal muscle work (fibres repeatedly contracting), not work on the suitcase. Physics work is done ON an object through displacement; physiological effort is not the same quantity.

questions.question: A brakes-applied car skids to a stop. Who does negative work, and what does negative work mean physically?
questions.solution: Friction acts opposite to displacement (θ = 180°, cosθ = −1), so friction does negative work — it REMOVES kinetic energy, converting it to heat. Negative work = energy taken from the object. The car's KE → thermal energy of tyres and road.

questions.question: State the work-energy theorem and use it to find the stopping distance when a 1000 kg car at 20 m/s is stopped by a 5000 N braking force.
questions.solution: Net work = change in KE: W = ½mv² − 0. Stopping distance d: −F·d = −½mv² → d = mv²/2F = (1000 × 400)/(2 × 5000) = 40 m. The theorem converts a force problem into an energy bookkeeping problem — no kinematics needed, and it generalises to varying forces.

questions.question: Why does gravity's work depend only on height change, while friction's work depends on the path taken?
questions.solution: Gravity is CONSERVATIVE: work done around any closed loop is zero, so only endpoints matter — it stores energy in a potential (mgh). Friction is non-conservative: the longer the path, the more work it dissipates as heat, and no potential can be assigned. Conservative forces ⇒ potential energy exists; that is the definition.

questions.question: Two cranes lift the same load to the same height; one takes 10 s, the other 40 s. Compare their work and power.
questions.solution: Work is identical — same force (weight) through the same displacement, W = mgh. Power = W/t differs by 4×: the fast crane delivers 4 times the power. Energy says HOW MUCH was transferred; power says HOW FAST — two independent ratings.

questions.concept: Why a pendulum conserves mechanical energy
questions.question: A swinging pendulum slows at the top and speeds at the bottom, yet total mechanical energy stays constant. Explain what is being exchanged.
questions.solution: Gravity is conservative, so the pendulum trades KE for PE continuously: at the extremes all energy is potential (mgh, v = 0); at the bottom all is kinetic (½mv², h minimal). The SUM stays fixed because the only force doing work (gravity) has a potential. With friction or air drag, mechanical energy would drain into heat and the sum would fall.

questions.question: Two pumps move the same water to the same tank; one takes 2 minutes, the other 8. Why is power the useful comparison and not work?
questions.solution: Both do identical WORK (same mass lifted through the same height), so work cannot separate them. Power = W/t differs 4× — the fast pump delivers energy 4 times faster, which is what matters for the job's throughput and for sizing the motor. Work tells you the total bill; power tells you the rate you must pay it.

questions.question: Why can no real machine convert all its input energy into useful output, and what happens to the rest?
questions.solution: Friction, air resistance, electrical resistance and sound all divert energy into thermal/sound forms that are not the intended output — the second law forbids fully ordered conversion. Efficiency = useful output/total input is therefore always < 1, and the 'lost' energy has not vanished: it has degraded into low-grade heat, spread into the surroundings.
